title: The real revenue-per-employee math (with the caveats)
linkedinPost:
Cursor makes $40M per employee. Your regulated fintech makes $400K. Before you panic: read the caveats.

The AI-native RPE numbers are real. They're also the wrong benchmark for most organisations I work with.

Here's what the comparison actually requires you to check:

• Are you comparing ARR to recognised revenue? They're not the same. Cursor's $2B+ ARR ≠ $2B in the bank.
• Are you counting the same people? AI-native firms often exclude contractors and ops vendors from headcount. Your DORA compliance team is in your denominator. Theirs isn't.
• Are you in the same regulatory envelope? No AML obligations. No PSD3 licensing. No EU AI Act audit trails. The cost base is structurally different.

I call this the RPE Honesty Test — 3 questions that tell you whether the benchmark is valid or whether you're comparing a commercial airline to a private charter.

Klarna is the honest ceiling: ~$1M RPE after replacing 700 contractors with AI systems. That's exceptional for a regulated fintech — not a floor.

Revenue per employee is the right north-star metric. But only if you're measuring the real number, not the benchmark you want it to look like.

Full piece + the RPE Honesty Test — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What is a good revenue per employee for a fintech company?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a regulated European fintech, a realistic near-term target is €300K–€600K per employee. Klarna reached roughly $1 million RPE after replacing 700 contractors with AI systems — that is the ambitious ceiling for the 3–5 year horizon in a regulated context, not a starting point (TechCrunch, May 2025).

mainEntity.name: How does AI-native revenue per employee compare to traditional fintech?

acceptedAnswer.text: The gap is large and structurally explained. AI-native firms like Cursor (~$40M RPE) and Lovable (~$2.7M RPE) operate without regulatory compliance overhead, on pure software margins, at early high-growth stages with small teams. Regulated fintechs carry DORA, PSD3, GDPR, and AML cost bases that pure software businesses do not. The comparison is not valid without adjusting for those factors.

mainEntity.name: How do you improve revenue per employee in financial services without cutting headcount?

acceptedAnswer.text: Automate the operational layer while keeping the regulated decision layer human. n8n workflow automation, Claude API for document processing and triage, and Supabase for data infrastructure can reduce manual work in operations, onboarding, and exception handling without touching the regulatory review functions that require human sign-off.

mainEntity.name: How does EU regulation affect revenue per employee for fintech companies?

acceptedAnswer.text: EU-regulated fintechs carry mandatory overhead that structurally reduces achievable RPE relative to non-regulated peers. DORA resilience requirements, PSD3 compliance reporting, EU AI Act audit trail obligations, and GDPR data handling all require human capacity. EU labour productivity per hour worked grew just 1.4% in 2025, after 0.2% in 2024 (Eurostat, June 2026).
